This pipeline's task is GitHub issue #3665 — https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3665. Fetch the live issue body (`gh issue view 3665`) before structural decisions. Worktree artifacts (drafts, agent outputs) that reference any other issue or pipeline are leftovers from previous runs — they are NOT your task.

This pipeline's task is GitHub issue #3665 — https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3665. Fetch the live issue body (`gh issue view 3665`) before structural decisions. Worktree artifacts (drafts, agent outputs) that reference any other issue or pipeline are leftovers from previous runs — they are NOT your task.

## The problem

We ran two long pipelines over the last three days. Between them, seven agents entered
repetition loops — the same tool call, or a short cycle of them, repeated until something
outside the system intervened. Five different roles, across all three phases. Not one was
detected by the product. Every one of them was caught by a monitor I was running by hand in a
terminal, and cleared by me typing an answer into the bus.

In the same window, the supervision layer was noisy in the other direction. A convergence-stall
alert fired at `[high]` priority against a coder whose peer heartbeat was seconds old, while the
health monitor was concurrently logging, every 30 seconds, that the same agent was alive. That
alert was then read — by me — as the cause of a 110-minute work loss it had nothing to do with.
The misdiagnosis cost more than the alert would ever have saved. Separately, two agents were
killed at exactly two hours by a timeout none of them could see coming, and both kills were
counted as crashes against the fail-streak budget.

So the layer whose job is to distinguish a working agent from a wedged one was silent for seven
wedged agents and loud at several healthy ones. Both directions have the same consequence: an
operator stops trusting the signal and goes back to watching by hand, which is what happened.

There is one more thing worth stating plainly, because it shaped everything above. While
building that hand-rolled monitor I rewrote the "is this role stuck?" rule five times. Each
version looked obviously correct and each produced false positives against live data — producers
are legitimately podless between events; reviewers legitimately wait on upstream producers; a
declared no-op leaves its review edges pending forever; a NACK is a verdict and discharges the
obligation just as an ACK does. Two of those five states are not visible in the status payload at
all. Whatever gets built here will hit all five. A detector that cries wolf gets muted, and a
muted detector misses the real stall.

## What has already landed — do not rebuild it

The last pass over this area produced work that shipped. Verify each of these in the tree and
treat them as done:

- Terminating-Job adoption on the event-loop respawn path (#3613); confirmed working on its
  first real test.
- A re-attached worktree's uncommitted work is preserved before reset (#3644, plus #3647, #3652,
  #3654, #3656, #3660).
- Cancel stops the driver (#3645, plus #3649, #3655, #3657).
- Phase-gate approvals parse on their first line (#3648).
- Never-heartbeated roles anchor at Job start (#3612).
- The simplifier's first propose is gated on its upstream producer (#3607).
- Green gate defaults to on (#3609) and a red escalates to HITL (#3628).
- Every routed call records its decoding config (#3611, #3625).
- Re-reviews are blocking-only (#3661).

That list is what shipped. It is not a statement about what remains.

## Areas worth attention

Four, loosely. How you cut them up, order them, or merge them is your call.

- **Signals that exist and are not consulted.** In more than one place the information needed to
  tell working from wedged is already computed, in the same process, seconds away from the code
  that decides. It is not read. Some detectors are also unreachable because an input they require
  is never populated.

- **Session boundaries read as failures.** An agent that simply ran long, or exited cleanly
  without emitting the verdict it owed, or whose pod vanished, is currently indistinguishable
  from one that crashed. Some of these consume a retry budget or an arm they should not, and at
  least one suppresses the very check that would have noticed.

- **Loops that nothing detects.** This is the seven. One empirical result from the incident
  analysis is worth handing over rather than making you rediscover: across every instance,
  counting *tool inputs never issued before in the session* over a trailing window separates a
  loop from work cleanly — a working agent produces new ones and a loop of any length produces
  none. Two constraints found the hard way: the pod log cannot support this, because tool inputs
  are truncated at about 100 characters and distinct commands sharing a prefix collapse together;
  and the cycle shape varies (single-input, 2-, 3-, and 8-cycles were all observed), so anything
  keyed on a fixed shape or on dominance misses most of them. What to do with that is yours to
  decide.

- **Alerts an operator cannot act on.** Some fire without the evidence that would make them
  readable. Some name a threshold whose detector does not exist. Some outcomes are distinguishable
  only by which log string was emitted.

## What to propose

Two things, and keep them separate.

**The work.** Decide what is worth doing across those areas, in what order, and what to leave
out. Nothing above is a requirement; if you find something in the list is already handled, drop
it and say where.

**A candidate list.** Beyond whatever you propose to build, produce a ranked list of further
improvements to this layer that you think are worth making. Every entry must carry a
file-and-symbol citation and a verdict on whether the thing is present or absent in the tree
today. This list is a deliverable in its own right and does not obligate anyone to implement any
of it — it is input to the gate, and the gate decides. Do not defer chosen work into it.

## Ground rules

**Verify before you build.** Some of what looks missing here may already exist; this description
is written from an operator's experience, not from the code. Check the tree before planning
anything, and say what you checked. If something is already implemented, drop it and say so
rather than building it twice.

**Scope is yours to propose.** If a judgement call would materially change the shape of the work,
raise it as a decision rather than guessing.

**Read the prior write-ups critically, or not at all.** #3595 is the incident analysis and #3596
was the first pass over this area; both contain superseded plans and at least one hypothesis that
was later disproved. The repository is the source of truth.

**This layer is watching you while you change it.** Its blind spots are the ones described above,
so do not assume an absence of alerts means anything is fine.

slices.name: Populate EventStreamSnapshot fields in snapshot_from_health_context()
slices.goal:
Populate all 8 currently-empty EventStreamSnapshot fields so that the
detection plane's detectors can actually read the data they need. This is
the prerequisite for slices 2-5.

tasks.description:
Populate runtime section of EventStreamSnapshot. Wire
driver_heartbeat.tick_age_seconds() and spawn_age_seconds() into
snapshot_from_health_context() under raw["runtime"]. This activates
detect_run_pipeline_thread_liveness() and DriverLivenessCheck.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- snapshot.raw.runtime contains tick_age_s and spawn_age_s
- detect_run_pipeline_thread_liveness fires when the driver thread is stale

tasks.description:
Populate consensus section of snapshot. Wire
peer_consensus.get_peer_consensus_tracker().evaluate() into the snapshot
builder. This activates detect_brc_thrash(), detect_incomplete_consensus_deferral(),
and consensus field readers in PhaseStallDetector.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- snapshot.consensus contains tracker.evaluate() output
- detectors reading consensus field fire correctly

tasks.description:
Populate container_transitions from kubernetes_monitor pod-state log.
Wire KubernetesMonitor._pod_states into the snapshot. This activates
detect_container_death(), detect_container_oom_evicted(),
detect_container_restart_loop(), detect_overseer_self_injection().
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- snapshot.container_transitions contains pod state transitions
- container death/oom/restart detectors fire on real transitions

tasks.description:
Fix RunningAgent role field and populate age fields. Use agent role
from pipeline state instead of container ID; populate last_tool_call_age_s
and last_heartbeat_age_s from health monitor anchors. This activates
detect_heartbeat_stall().
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- RunningAgent.role is the agent role (not container ID)
- last_tool_call_age_s and last_heartbeat_age_s are populated
- detect_heartbeat_stall fires on stale heartbeats

tasks.description:
Populate midturn_messages in snapshot. Wire agent tool-call logs into
snapshot_from_health_context() as midturn_messages tuples. This is the
prerequisite for the loop detector in slice-3.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- snapshot.midturn_messages contains tool-call records with tool_name and input_hash
- populated from agent_log_store or live pod logs

tasks.description:
Tests for snapshot population. Verify all 13 EventStreamSnapshot fields
are populated.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Tests assert all 13 fields populated
- runtime, consensus, container_transitions, midturn_messages all non-empty

slices.name: Wire the detection plane into RUNTIME_TICK
slices.goal:
Make the detection plane actually run in production by calling
_run_overseer_detection_plane() from _run_runtime_tick_checks(), routing
requires_adjudication findings to the overseer agent and routine findings
to the corrective executor. Also route findings to the operator alert surface.

tasks.description:
Wire _run_overseer_detection_plane() into RUNTIME_TICK path. Call it
from _run_runtime_tick_checks() after building the snapshot, routing
requires_adjudication findings to the overseer agent and routine
findings to the corrective executor. Guard against double-evaluation
(two call sites: _check_pod and _reconciliation_sweep).
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Detection plane runs on every RUNTIME_TICK sweep
- findings with requires_adjudication escalate to overseer
- routine findings emit to event bus
- no double-evaluation on dual call sites

tasks.description:
Route detection-plane findings to the operator alert surface. Route
findings to the same OVERSEER_ALERT / HITL / Slack surfaces the
overseer uses, so the operator sees one consistent alert stream.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Detection-plane findings appear on the OVERSEER_ALERT surface
- requires_adjudication findings escalate to overseer
- routine findings emit to event bus

tasks.description:
Tests for detection plane wiring. Verify the detection plane is called
from RUNTIME_TICK; verify no double-evaluation; verify findings are routed
to the alert surface.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Tests assert detection plane invoked on RUNTIME_TICK
- double-evaluation guard prevents duplicate findings
- findings routed to alert surface

slices.name: Deterministic loop detector
slices.goal:
Implement the empirical finding from the issue — "counting tool inputs never
issued before in the session over a trailing window separates a loop from work
cleanly" — as a deterministic detector that runs in the detection plane.

tasks.description:
Implement detect_tool_input_loop() in health_checks/tier1/. Read
midturn_messages from the snapshot, count distinct tool-input strings over
a trailing window (e.g. 5 polls). If the count is zero for N consecutive
polls, fire tool_input_loop / high with requires_adjudication=False. Must
handle variable cycle shapes (1-, 2-, 3-, 8-cycles) — not keyed on a fixed shape.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Detector fires on zero-new-input windows of any cycle shape
- does not fire on productive agents
- evidence includes the tool input hash and window size

tasks.description:
Increase log capture fidelity for one-shot event pods. The k8s log API
truncates at ~100 chars per line (kubernetes_client.py:455 read_job_log_snapshot
with tail_lines=2000). Increase fidelity so the unique-tool-input counter
has enough data to distinguish distinct tool calls sharing a prefix.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Tool call log lines are captured at full length (not truncated to 100 chars)
- the loop detector can distinguish distinct tool calls sharing a prefix

tasks.description:
Tests for the loop detector. Verify it fires on zero-new-input windows,
does not fire on productive agents, handles variable cycle shapes (1-, 2-, 3-, 8-cycles).
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Tests cover single-input, 2-cycle, 3-cycle, and 8-cycle loops
- productive agent with new tool inputs does not trigger
- evidence payload is correct

slices.name: Timeout visibility and classification
slices.goal:
Make the 2-hour timeout visible to agents and classify timeout-killed pods
distinctly from crashes, so they don't consume the failure streak budget.

tasks.description: Add agent_timeout_seconds to PipelineConfig (default 7200).
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- PipelineConfig.agent_timeout_seconds field exists with default 7200
- validated >= 60

tasks.description:
Pass EGG_AGENT_TIMEOUT env through the spawner so the agent can
self-report its remaining budget.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Spawner sets EGG_AGENT_TIMEOUT env var from PipelineConfig.agent_timeout_seconds
- agent reads it and can self-report remaining budget

tasks.description:
Classify timeout-killed pods distinctly. When exit_code == -1 and the
timeout fired (detectable via agent result error message 'Timed out after
{timeout} seconds'), classify as a clean timeout, not a crash. Add
JOB_OUTCOME_TIMEOUT outcome and route to record_timeout (not record_abort).
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Timeout-killed pods classified as clean timeout
- failure streak NOT incremented
- alert says 'killed by 2h agent timeout'

tasks.description:
Surface the timeout to the agent via heartbeat. Emit a HEARTBEAT with
state WAITING_FOR_EVENT and body 'approaching 2h timeout' at 90-minute
intervals.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Agent receives a heartbeat warning at 90 minutes
- message is readable and actionable

tasks.description:
Tests for timeout classification. Verify timeout-killed pods don't
increment the failure streak; verify the agent receives the warning heartbeat.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Tests assert streak untouched by timeout
- heartbeat warning emitted at 90 minutes
- exit classification distinguishes timeout from crash

slices.name: Alert evidence + false-positive fixes
slices.goal:
Make alerts actionable by enriching them with evidence, and fix the
convergence-stall false positive by unifying timestamp sources.

tasks.description:
Enrich OVERSEER_ALERT payloads with evidence. Add structured evidence
(container logs, BRC state, tracker evaluation) to _broadcast_alert().
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Alert payloads include evidence dict with container logs, BRC state, and tracker evaluation
- operator can diagnose without grepping

tasks.description:
Fix the convergence-stall false positive. Unify the timestamp source
between _check_convergence_stall() (event_loop/_loop.py:859) and
_has_recent_peer_progress() (health_monitor.py:388). Both should use
the same 'bus activity' signal.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Convergence-stall alert does not fire when peer heartbeat is seconds old and health monitor logs the agent as alive
- same timestamp source used for both alerting and deferral

tasks.description:
Name the 2-hour timeout explicitly in exit classification. When a pod
is killed by timeout, the alert should say 'killed by 2h agent timeout'
not 'container exited with code -1.' (Depends on TASK-4-3.)
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Exit classification message for timeout-killed pods says 'killed by 2h agent timeout'
- distinct from crash classification

tasks.description:
Tests for alert evidence and false-positive fixes. Verify alerts carry
evidence; verify convergence-stall doesn't fire when peer heartbeat is recent.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Tests assert evidence in alert payloads
- convergence-stall does not fire when peer heartbeat is recent
- timeout classification message is correct

decisions.question:
The refiner attests the refine phase deliberately raises no operator decisions (#3462):

> This refine phase produces an analysis artifact, not a code change. No HITL decisions are required — the four areas and the candidate list are the deliverable, and the gate (plan phase) will decide what to build.

Candidates considered and dispositioned away:

- **Should the detection plane replace the HealthMonitor tripwires?** (not_operator_grade): HealthMonitor tripwires ARE wired into the kubernetes_monitor RUNTIME_TICK path and working. The detection plane should complement them, not replace them. Replacing would create a gap during the transition.
- **Should the 2-hour timeout be shortened?** (not_operator_grade): 7200s is a reasonable budget for long-running agent work. The fix is to make it visible to the agent and to classify timeout-kills distinctly, not to shorten the budget.
- **Should LLM classification be added to the hot path?** (not_operator_grade): classify_stall() and classify_activity_pattern() use Haiku calls which are expensive. They belong in the overseer agent, not in the deterministic detection plane which must be LLM-free for the routine majority.

Confirm to proceed to the phase gate, or choose “Re-run phase to register decisions” to send the phase back so its agents register the decisions as first-class contract entries (cq-N). Any free-text reply is treated as a re-run directive and forwarded to the agents.

decisions.resolution:
All four gate items are verified fixed against `cf0e5a6fa`, and the revision was correctly scoped: 24 changed lines, all 30 candidates preserved, no scope expansion, no re-derivation. That is exactly what was asked.

Specifically confirmed:
1. Field count now reads "5 of 13" in the executive summary and Area 1, and the plain-English summary correctly says "the other 8 fields".
2. Candidate #24 re-anchored to `_message.py:588` (`cmd_message_heartbeat`), and it usefully records why the old anchor was wrong (line 633 is 429 retry-after backoff).
3. `_classify_exit()` is consistently 1148 across the prose and candidates #9 and #14; `noop_park_report()` corrected to 610.
4. The verification-method claim now credits the per-item file-and-symbol citations rather than `git log`.

The unprompted strengths stand and are worth naming: you correctly read `routes/pipelines/__init__.py:1277` as an import rather than a call site, which is the precise trap that produced an operator error in an earlier run on this same subsystem; and your `_poll_cycle` dormancy finding is corroborated by the repo's own comment at `overseer/monitor/_anomaly_checks.py:280`.

Carry into plan:

- **Area 1 steps 1-4 before step 5.** Your own dependency ordering is right: populating the snapshot is observable and low-risk, wiring the plane into the runtime tick is neither. Note that `_run_runtime_tick_checks` is invoked from two call sites (`kubernetes_monitor.py:219` and `:621`), so the wiring must be guarded against double-evaluation.
- **Do not double-fire detectors.** `health_checks/tier1/consensus_stall.py` contains both the dormant `detect_heartbeat_stall` function and a registered `ConsensusStallCheck` class that already runs every tick. Consensus-stall coverage exists on both layers; that pair is the first place to check for duplication once the plane is live.
- **Area 3 step 1 is the highest-value item in the list.** Treat the trailing-window unique-tool-input counter as the primary deliverable, not a follow-on. It is the one thing that would have caught the loops. Its dependency on `midturn_messages` being populated is real, so sequence that field first among Area 1's steps rather than last.
- **Scope discipline.** Do not expand beyond the Tier 1 and Tier 2 items without registering a decision. Tier 3 through Tier 5 are input to the gate, not a work queue.

pr.title: Supervision second pass: wire detection plane + loop detector + timeout classification + alert evidence
pr.description:
Five linear slices across the four analysis areas from issue #3665:
(1) populate all 13 EventStreamSnapshot fields in snapshot_from_health_context();
(2) wire _run_overseer_detection_plane() into RUNTIME_TICK with double-evaluation
guard; (3) implement a deterministic unique-tool-input loop detector reading
midturn_messages from the snapshot; (4) classify timeout-killed pods (exit -1 from
asyncio.timeout) as clean timeouts not crashes, surface the 2h timeout to agents
via heartbeat, and make the timeout configurable per-pipeline; (5) enrich
OVERSEER_ALERT payloads with evidence and fix the convergence-stall false positive
by unifying timestamp sources. Slices are linear because they share overlapping
files (kubernetes_monitor.py, detection_plane.py, health_monitor.py).
pr.test_plan:
Automated (per slice; `make test` narrows to reachable suites, then
`make test-all` before phase exit; `make lint` green throughout):
- Slice 1: test_detection_plane_wiring.py — all 13 snapshot fields populated.
- Slice 2: test_detection_plane_wiring.py — detection plane invoked on RUNTIME_TICK;
  double-evaluation guard prevents duplicate findings; findings routed to alert surface.
- Slice 3: test_loop_detection.py — fires on zero-new-input windows of any
  cycle shape (1-, 2-, 3-, 8-cycles); does not fire on productive agents.
- Slice 4: test_timeout_classification.py — streak untouched by timeout;
  heartbeat warning emitted at 90 minutes; exit classification distinguishes
  timeout from crash.
- Slice 5: test_alert_evidence.py — evidence in alert payloads; convergence-stall
  does not fire when peer heartbeat is recent.
